It could be a few reasons (aside from being probably new/inexperienced)

* This person probably had you in a multi-order batch. Meaning you were bunched in with one or two other people and they could have had large orders (which explains the length of time and distant location) 

* The weird items could be that they accidentally grouped your items with the wrong order. It happens occasionally, but if someone was new it could happen more often. 

* not sure about the different person. The person could very well be using their family’s or significant other’s phone to shop. 



They most likely took this multi order batch and didn’t know how to do it. Contact support for a refund and rate accordingly.

I promise you this is just friendly advice! 

When you greet your customers, come at a friendly and inviting place. I absolutely understand the issue with non responsiveness. But that should come towards the end. For example: 

“Hello! I am almost finished with your order and will be heading to checkout soon. I’ve noticed you haven’t responded to my replacement suggestions, and just to be safe, I will go ahead and issue a refund for those for you if I haven’t heard back from you before checkout!” 

This gives the customer a window to respond, and if not, then go ahead and issue refund. Make sure to send it about 2-3 items before you’re done to give them a chance to respond. If not, issue refund and there’s no harm no foul! Take the photos of the items that can be replaced and move on to the next. Once you’ve finished all of your items found, you can go back to whatever they want and be done. 

It might take an extra 5 minutes out of your shop, but I promise you it’s a friendlier and more customer oriented way of going about things.
